findings.reason: a plan that converges "one reader of section boundaries" must name the existing section-text readers it is not reusing, or it rebuilds them unwittingly.
findings.text: §16 builds prose extraction from `_TAG_RE` but never cites `reckon/mcp_views.py:2061 authored_plan_text` ("searchable prose while excluding Reckon's structured collections") or `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:308 _plan_section_text` ("Extract one section's visible text without including its successors"), both of which already do the job the new `strip_tags` + span slice is introduced for

findings.reason: two section-text readers over the same spans drift exactly as the heading walks did before §17, and §16's own premise is that one owner should read section boundaries.
findings.text: once §16 is built the package carries two owners of one section's text from a plan document: the new `_authored_prose`-over-spans slicer in `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` and `dispatch._plan_section_text`, which already slices `plan_headings` spans and pulls text the same way; the plan should extend/hoist `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` (or state why a separate reader is required) rather than add a third

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §16 adds one module-private mapping (`_section_digests`), one private coverage predicate and one public pure function (`strip_tags`), while deleting `_AuthoredProseParser` and the gate's duplicate whole-document read, so the added interface is smaller than the behaviour it hides.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §16 lands a section-scoped prose slicer by rewriting `_authored_prose` to slice `structured_section_spans` spans and strip tags, beside the live `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:308 _plan_section_text`, which already extracts one section's visible text from the raw document using the same `plan_headings` spans; the plan names no owner to extend.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1480, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 accounts for its one public addition (`strip_tags`, 1480→1481), retires the public `legacy` keyword from `plan_fingerprint`, reuses the plan-review-missing refusal family, and §20 adds nothing.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §16 adds a per-section prose extractor without citing the two existing extractors that already read authored plan text, `reckon/mcp_views.py:2061 authored_plan_text` and `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:308 _plan_section_text`; the plan cites `_TAG_RE` but names neither, so its reuse map is incomplete for the mechanism it adds.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — `strip_tags` is not a pass-through (it removes skipped-element interiors, unescapes entities and collapses whitespace), `structured_section_spans(every_marked_element=…)` is a keyword on an existing reader rather than a wrapper, and §16 states in-text why the coverage predicate is not a wrapper over `read_plan_review`.
